item.title: Version 1.1.0.6
item.description:
Thank you to everyone sending feedback. The permission fix below came straight from a Reddit comment.

  • Chinese and Japanese in terminals. FlowIn now understands input method composition: ghost text hides while you type pinyin or romaji, and the suggestion appears right when the text commits. CJK suggestions sit exactly on the terminal grid, iTerm2 no longer shows phantom spaces between characters, and the cursor position is right on CJK lines in Otty.
  • Permission self-heal. macOS can silently invalidate FlowIn's Accessibility permission after an update, while System Settings still shows it enabled. FlowIn now detects this at launch, after wake, and within a minute mid-session, walks you through the fix, and reconnects automatically.
  • Flow Draft understands WeChat drafts. If you have already typed part of a message, a right Option tap now refines your draft instead of replying to it, and rewrite options lead with Humanize.
  • New controls. Auto-show for Word Alternatives is now a switch in Settings, off by default; the shortcut still opens the menu anytime. Clipboard Context gets its own toggle, and Screen Context flips with a switch right in the menu bar.
  • Fixes. Suggestions land at the cursor on a display positioned left of your main one, the alternatives menu stays quiet in CJK text and right after numbers, and hidden overlay panels no longer intercept clicks.

item.title: Version 1.1.0.5
item.description:
Thank you to everyone who has been sending feedback through Discord, email, WeChat, etc. Much of this update came straight from it.

  • More apps. FlowIn now works in Cursor and Obsidian, and Claude Code sessions are recognized in iTerm2 and Otty, not just Terminal. In Cursor, suggestions stay out of the code editor and the integrated terminal.
  • Better in terminals. Accepting is much faster over a long scrollback, and suggestions line up with the cursor. At a plain shell prompt FlowIn now stays quiet, so Tab still runs your shell's own completion.
  • Smarter word units. Tab accepts one segment at a time in compounds like well-known and paths like src/main.swift, and stops flush before punctuation.
  • A clearer first run. A model download that outlives setup now shows a progress card, a percentage in the menu bar, and a retry if it fails.
  • Various improvements. Settings follows light mode and supports Cmd+Z, the menu bar gains an Upgrade entry and tells you when the daily free limit is reached, suggestions no longer blink while you type, the Word Alternatives menu closes when you switch desktops, and Notion no longer joins words together.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
First, thank you to everyone testing FlowIn and sending feedback. This is our biggest update yet.

  • Word Alternatives. While a suggestion is showing, a small menu appears under the ghost text with other ways to continue. Pick with arrow keys, digit keys, or Tab, and FlowIn continues from your choice.
  • Flow Draft. Our reply feature, now with a name and more power: tap the right Option key to draft a reply, or select any text to rewrite it. Drafts are generated in the cloud, and your content is never stored.
  • Autocomplete now runs fully on your Mac. Suggestions come from the on-device model: fast, private, and works offline. (If you previously used a cloud model for autocomplete, FlowIn switches to the on-device model automatically.)
  • A new guided setup. Download the on-device model, learn the shortcuts, and try Flow Draft before you start writing.
  • Plans and a free trial. New installs start a 14-day Pro trial with unlimited autocomplete. Afterwards FlowIn continues on the free plan, and you can upgrade anytime in Settings.
  • Quality of life. Usage dashboard in Settings, words-saved count in the menu bar, launch at login, timed disable, Join Discord in the menu bar, and dozens of reliability fixes.

item.title: Version 1.0.7
item.description:
First of all, thanks for everyone's support and feedback. Your enthusiasm for FlowIn is something I really didn't expect, and I'm grateful that FlowIn is helping with your daily writing, even in a small way.

Our goal is really to make it much easier to express your intent, and we've been working day and night to make that happen. This update has a few major features I'm excited to share.

  • Draft a full reply anywhere. Tap the right Option (⌥) key in any app, pick a direction, and FlowIn writes the whole reply in your voice.
  • A much faster, smoother local model.
  • Updated shortcuts. Tab accepts word by word, the backtick key (`) accepts the whole suggestion, and right-Command + ↑/↓ cycles alternatives.

item.title: Version 1.0.6.1
item.description:
• Significantly improved Fast model performance, now it is the default model
  • New onboarding step: an "About you" profile that tailors suggestions to how you write
  • Suggestions now default to Phrase length
  • Better Chinese and Japanese input: accept suggestions one character at a time, with smoother overlap handling for non-Latin scripts
  • Longer suggestions can extend one line below the input box
  • Fixes: steadier insertion in Safari, accurate caret alignment in terminals, and fewer duplicated characters

item.title: Version 1.0.6
item.description:
• Cycle through 3 alternative suggestions with right-Option + ⌥↓ / ⌥↑ after a partial accept
  • Screen context: keeps OCR fresh during typing, better sender attribution in chat bubbles
  • Onboarding: new keyboard graphics for permission steps and an interactive cycle tutorial
  • App now requires an invite code on first launch — contact us if you need one
  • Fixes around 3-in-1 cycle parsing and special-character edge cases

item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
• Suggestions stay aligned even after pasting, deleting, or inserting ChatGPT/Telegram conversation snippets
  • Ghost text now stays put on the active Space and renders over app launchers (Raycast, Spotlight, etc.) instead of disappearing
  • Fewer false-fire suggestions: skip when caret has no preceding text after a click, skip when prefix ends with "?", arrow keys no longer trigger inference, selection mode hides ghost text
  • Onboarding step 2 reveal animation + softer pill buttons
  • DMG now uses drag-to-install layout with an arrow guide

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description: • Auto-update prompts now reliably come to the front so you don't miss them

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description:
• New first-launch onboarding with permissions setup and an interactive tutorial page
  • Redesigned Settings window with auto-saving User Context, scrollable layout, and new "AI Models" and "Suggestion Length" sections
  • Local model significantly improved across quality, latency, and reliability
  • Better support for typing in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean
  • Fixed text insertion edge cases around word boundaries, special characters, and Gmail quoted replies
  • Autocomplete now starts disabled in IDEs on first install (toggle per-app from the menu)

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
• Ghost text now dismisses cleanly on Return, Cmd+A, forward delete, and Emacs-style keybindings
  • Improved ghost text dismissal in search fields and on paste/cut
  • Fixed a crash in text measurement (Double-to-Int overflow)
  • Faster context reads (capped at ~8K chars)

item.title: Version 1.0.1
item.description:
• Fixed text insertion in Gmail replies with quoted history
  • Added support for terminal emulators (iTerm2, Warp, ghostty, kitty, etc.)
  • Fixed rapid word-by-word acceptance occasionally duplicating words
  • Fixed crash when Chrome's accessibility state became temporarily invalid
  • Detect limited browsers (Firefox/Arc) and show an inline hint

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
• Rebranded to FlowIn
  • Improved permission prompts for Screen Context
  • Fixed reliability issues (secure input, sleep/wake, App Nap)
  • Better suggestion display in Outlook and WKWebView apps
  • Smart ghost text persistence on space and delete
  • Clipboard session management for rapid Tab acceptance
  • Redesigned toolbar with collapsible FlowIn widget
  • Timed disable options (15m, 60m, indefinitely)
  • Auto-update support via Sparkle
